title: Duplicate Distractor Analysis

severity_thresholds.critical: 100% identical text across >= 3 items (certification-blocking per D4 < 2)

critical_findings.group: DL-012 Clone Group — Pack C Section C items CC-021 through CC-027
critical_findings.text: it guarantees goal congruence in all cases
critical_findings.items: All Unprocessed — not yet in learner pool but blocks certification
critical_findings.remediation: Each item needs a distinct, choice-specific replacement. S90 rewrites already proposed for 6 of 7.

critical_findings.group: DL-012 Clone Group — Pack C/D Section E clone-archived items
critical_findings.text: Various — 28 groups × 2-5 items with rotation artifacts
critical_findings.items: Archived — not in learner pool. DL-012 remediation plan documented.
critical_findings.remediation: Per-group audit required. Clone groups share stem structure but have different correct answers.

cross_pack_similarity.finding: 56 cross-pack duplicate groups detected. Most are legitimate — same concept tested with same distractors across packs for consistency. However, when one pack has strong ExplanationWrong and another has boilerplate for the SAME distractor text, this is asymmetric quality.
cross_pack_similarity.example: Same distractor text appears in Pack A Section A (with choice-specific EW) and Pack C Section D (with DL-013 boilerplate EW) — Candidate B gets better feedback than Candidate A for the same wrong answer.

pack_most_affected: Pack D — 91 boilerplate EW fields. Highest concentration of DL-013 'represents a plausible misconception' template text in non-Certified sections (E and F).
